Subject: Update from Cascade Legal Rights Project

We understand why people are concerned. Getting a letter from a lawyer after asking for help can be frightening, and it’s reasonable to ask how personal information is handled.

Cascade Legal Rights Project does not provide clinic attendees’ information to landlords or their attorneys. We do not share, sell, or disclose attendee information for that purpose. Sign-in records are kept internally in locked storage.

There may be another explanation for the letters: eviction filings in Magistrate Court are public records, and some firms use those records to send mailings to tenants. We can’t determine the source of any particular letter, and we won’t discuss anyone’s individual situation here.

The free tenant rights clinic is still happening this Saturday, November 14, from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m. The library room is closed, so we’ve moved the clinic to Mt Zion Fellowship Hall. The accessible entrance is the side entrance by the parking lot. No appointment is needed, and you are welcome to come.

Questions? Email clinic@cascaderights.example or call our office at 404-555-0187. We appreciate people raising concerns and want everyone to have clear information before deciding whether to attend.
